title: The pH Scale
text: The pH scale measures how acidic or basic (alkaline) a water-based solution is, ranging from 0 to 14. A pH of 7 is neutral (pure water); values below 7 are acidic (e.g., lemon juice, stomach acid); values above 7 are basic (e.g., baking soda, soap). The scale is logarithmic, so each whole-number change represents a tenfold change in hydrogen ion concentration. pH is critical in biology, agriculture, medicine, and industrial chemistry.
